A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SCG/OSCMWU work. Their main texts, tables, equations and Appendices A–G are readable and matchable despite reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 presents mathematical applications, complexity bounds and proofs, including in its appendices, but reports no original experimental or simulation outcomes.

after.justification: v4 Sections 6.1–6.2 and Figures 1–3 report original simulations for Iris metric learning, synthetic facility location and streaming facility location.

M1.justification: The OSCMWU accumulation rule, optimistic predictor, exponential map and trace normalization are unchanged. The streaming experiment instantiates the existing online update with time-varying payoffs.

E1.justification: v2 only develops theoretical application formulations. v4 adds actual evaluation on Iris and synthetic facility-location instances, plus a distinct streaming-demand scenario with temporally correlated inputs.

E2.justification: SCMWU becomes an actually evaluated comparator in all three new experiments. v2 discusses SCMWU and other algorithms through theoretical bounds and related work, without measured comparisons; the new empirical comparator set remains limited to SCMWU.

E3.justification: v4 introduces experimental protocols: 9,000 Iris iterations with stepsize 20, 10,000 static facility-location iterations with stepsize 0.07, and 20,000 streaming rounds with stepsize 10. Evaluation uses averaged-iterate duality gaps, objective values and time-scaled regrets. These are new protocols, not revisions to existing v2 experiments.

E4.justification: The new comparisons provide a limited ablation of optimism: Section 4 identifies SCMWU as the zero-predictor case, and Section 6 compares it with OSCMWU using matched stepsizes and budgets. No broader sensitivity sweeps or dedicated robustness studies are added.

E5.justification: v4 introduces mean curves and shaded bands of plus or minus one standard deviation over five independent seeds in Figures 1–3, with descriptions of what seeds resample. v2 contains no corresponding statistical reporting; this is first reporting, not an increase from a previously stated run count.

E6.justification: Figures 1–3 add measured convergence findings: a modest Iris duality-gap advantage, substantially smaller static facility-location gaps, and lower streaming time-scaled regrets for OSCMWU relative to SCMWU. These are newly reported results; v2 has no empirical scores or curves to update.

T1.justification: Appendix C.3 corrects the missing one-half factor in the Pinsker step (v2 Equation 17; v4 Equation 19), changes erroneous i<i summation indices to i<j, and corrects the automorphism argument's condition from omega=e to omega squared=e. The main strong-convexity and convergence bounds remain unchanged.

C1.justification: v4 removes the assertion that the convergence rate is optimal from the abstract, contribution list and conclusion. It also qualifies the introduction's projection-free wording as avoiding Euclidean projection. The central SCG framework, OSCMWU algorithm and strong-convexity contributions are retained.

C2.justification: v4 interprets the new facility-location curves as supporting convergence and the streaming comparison as illustrating optimism's benefit under predictable demands. However, its invocation of Theorem 10 for the streaming experiment is not accompanied by an extension of Appendix D.1's fixed-game proof to changing demands.

D1.justification: v4 adds substantial simulation documentation: scikit-learn loading and standardization of Iris, pair sampling, dimensions, constraint radii, synthetic-data generation, initialization, stepsizes and iteration budgets. The streaming recipe specifies matrix normalization and AR(1) parameters. The existing exponential-computation discussion in Appendix B.4 is retained.

R1.justification: v4 adds Chen and Pan (2010) to distinguish prior strict convexity from strong convexity, references supporting quadratic-voting and beamforming examples, and Iris/scikit-learn citations. Existing positioning relative to SCMWU, OFTRL and optimistic quantum-game methods is largely retained.

P1.justification: v4 moves individual regret and strong convexity from Section 4 into a reorganized Section 5 with three subsections. It expands the ball-strategy example and edits contribution statements, conclusion and front matter, while retaining most existing exposition and appendix structure.

P2.justification: v4 adds three convergence figures containing four panels, with legends, logarithmic scales and uncertainty bands. It also adopts TMLR formatting with a redesigned author block, running headers, changed typography and wider text layout. Tables 1–2 are retained and reformatted.

improvement.justification: The new empirical illustrations with five-seed variability reporting, narrower convergence claims and local proof corrections provide a limited net improvement. The main theoretical contribution was already present. Comparisons remain confined to SCMWU, and the streaming experiment's appeal to the fixed-game regret theorem remains unjustified for changing demands.
